text:
alexa: quick follow-up to CP separation RFC — thinking about a hybrid model: short-lived regional anchors for control traffic + persistent per-tenant egress relays for IP-whitelisting customers. open to thoughts.
mike: makes sense as a tradeoff. anchors give us fast failover and lower blast radius; relays satisfy compliance (stable egress IPs). main ops cost is extra NAT state and SNAT table pressure for relays.
rana: agree. can we make relay mode opt-in per route? some customers need only embeddings routed via relays, not all traffic. that would limit cost.
alexa: yes — route-level mode is the idea: controlplane state goes to anchors, data-plane routes optionally pinned to relays. discovery complexity increases though.
mike: discovery options: (1) single DNS name that returns SRV records for anchors and relays (2) small registry service in controlplane that returns preferred endpoints per-customer (3) env/file override for Private installs. SRV is simplest for hosted.
rana: SRV TTL churn is a concern for low-latency clients. Also private installs can't always hit public DNS. need a clear fallback order in SDK.
alexa: proposal for client discovery priority: explicit env override -> local registry file/socket -> controlplane registry API -> DNS SRV -> fixed global fallback. timeouts: 30ms, 60ms, 200ms, 400ms, 1000ms respectively.
mike: SDK should expose those defaults and allow ops to tune. also add a small "prefer_relay_for_routes": ["/inference/stream","/embed"] flag so apps can opt routes into relay mode.
rana: streaming note: relays are better for sticky sessions, anchors better for control. for LLM streaming we need resumable sessions. suggest session tokens that embed anchor_id or relay_id and permit resume within TTL. tokens revocable on handoff.
alexa: agree. also we need a minimal handoff protocol: DRAIN_START window where writes are mirrored or temporarily accepted by both old+new for X seconds, then switch authoritative. ops must be able to force-cutover with a documented risk.
mike: caching: KV prefix cache must be prewarmed on the new anchor/relay to avoid huge cold-start latencies. two options: replicate full hot-set proactively, or prefetch top-N prefixes async. for most customers prefetch of top-200 prefixes should cover 80% of hits.
rana: bandwidth estimate request: top-200 prefixes ~= 25-50MB depending on model; ops please validate against telemetry. make prewarm optional in Private to avoid billing surprises.
alexa: security: for short-lived anchors we can use a central signer issuing leaf certs. for Private/offline installs offer an "offline bundle" CLI flow where customers upload signed bundles with explicit expiry. bundles must include serial and CRL support for revocation.
mike: revocation in air-gapped setups is hard. include a bundle serial check and allow ops to bump serial + force a short grace window during scheduled rotations. document clock-skew caveats.
rana: metrics/tracing: add tags anchor_id/relay_id, metric cp.handoff.duration, relay.snat_pressure, stream.resume_success. logs should include bundle_serial when present.
ops-bot: perf-spike scheduled: relay vs anchor egress for streaming workloads — Thu 09:00 UTC. please add test cases for hot-cache vs cold-bootstrap.
alexa: UX: console should show for each customer: current connect_mode (auto|anchor|relay), active_anchor_id(s), active_relay_id(s), last_handoff_time, bundle_serial (if private). include ops button to start maintenance/drain.
mike: one more thing: consider QUIC for direct anchor connections — improves resume across migrations. downside: QUIC middlebox compatibility and SDK complexity. probably opt-in for now.
alexa: action items: 1) mike + rana draft SDK discovery/fallback contract + config defaults, 2) ops to validate prewarm bandwidth numbers and run perf spike, 3) security to write offline-bundle lifecycle doc (cert serials/CRL), 4) product to spec console ops surface.
mike: I'll prototype SRV + registry fallback in SDK this week.
rana: will run bandwidth estimate and sample telemetry by EOD Fri.
alexa: thanks — capturing for RFC follow-up. leaving thread open for comments. :thumbsup:
